text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FRONT PAGE POLITICAL NEWS RZECZPOSPOLITA

- Poland, Germany and the Czech republic will consider co-operation in regulating the Oder River to prevent flooding in the future, Poland's Interior Minister Leszek Miller and the Brandenburg province Prime Minister Manfred Stolpe said. The EU is interested in supporting the programme.

- Poland's employers federation (KPP) has proposed launching an employers' aid fund to help flood victims. Financial assistance from the fund will support institutions and private persons, KPP's president Wojciech Kornowski said.
ECONOMIC AND MARKET STORIES RZECZPOSPOLITA

- Despite the Treasury Ministry's promise to produce a privatisation timetable for the Telekomunikacja Polska SA (TPSA) telecoms monopolist by the end of July the timetable will be presented around September at the earliest, a source who declined to be named said.

- Poland's average monthly salary in June 1997 was 27.1 percent higher than in the same period last year, the Central Statistical Office (GUS) said. The average salary's purchasing power in the first half of 1997 was higher than in the first six months o f 1996, GUS said.

- Broad money increased by 3.2 percent in the first 20 days of July showing the biggest growth this year, the National Bank of Poland (NBP), the central bank said. In the period from January 1 to July 20, 1997, broad money grew by 15 percent.

- The Filar insurance firm will pay 10 million zlotys in an advance damage payment to the Opole heating and power plant in south-western Poland to preserve the plant's liquidity as it repairs damages caused by recent floods.
- The Ariadna thread maker in Lodz, central Poland, showed a stable 30 percent annual sales growth for the last two years and a 100 percent net profit growth each year over the period, Ariadna said.

- The Altra Group leasing firm presented a share issue prospectus to the Polish Securities Commission (KPW) in the end of June, 1997. The firm had a net profit of 3.5 million zlotys on sales of 19.4 million zlotys in 1996, Altra Group said.
- The TU Compensa SA insurance firm made a net profit of 1.18 million zlotys in the first half of 1997 showing a 76 percent growth compared with the same period last year, Compensa said.
- Kredyt Bank has bought a 26 percent stake in the TUnZ Polisa Zycie life insurer, the bank announced. The value of the purchase was not disclosed.

- The crisis of Poland's insurance firms resulting from extensive flood damages will open new opportunities to international insurers interested in investing in the country's insurance industry, the Kjoebenhavnske Re reinsurence firm's president Leif Cor inth Hansen said.
DZIENNIK PRAWA I GOSPODARKI

- The listed Optimus computer hardware and software maker is extensively moving into areas of computer-related appliances which will account for 58 percent of the firm's sales in 1998, the Optimus president Roman Kluska said.
- The state-owned Porty Lotnicze airport management firm has bought into the SPL Mazurek-Szczytno local airport operator in north-eastern Poland, Porty Lotnicze said.
- Over 200,000 people are busy in Poland's direct marketing sector half of whom do it as a part-time job, a report by the Polish Direct Marketing Association said.

- Petrochemia Plock (PP), the country's biggest refinery will launch hydrocracking facilities by August 15, 1997, to increase the output of the low-sulphur lead-free fuels, the plant's development director Czeslaw Bugaj said.

- The Krotoszyn municipality in western Poland will shortly issue six-year munibonds worth 2.25 million zlotys, five-year bonds worth 2 million zlotys, four-year bonds worth 1.75 million zlotys and three-year bonds worth 1 million zlotys, the Krotoszyn authorities announced.
GAZETA WYBORCZA

- The formation of a shipbuilding holding including the Szczecin and Gdynia shipyards and the Hipolit Cegielski (HCP) ship engine maker has not taken place yet as the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) made no binding decisions on participation in the holding, the Economy Minister Wieslaw Kaczmarek said.
- The US's United Cinemas International (UCI) network will build 10 large-screen cinemas around Poland in the next three years worth $100 million, the network's deputy president Ray Smith said.
